key_insight: There is no universally best flow surrogate: the right architecture depends on whether the target dynamics are boundary-driven or self-sustained, especially under time-varying boundary conditions.
engineering_relevance: For CFD workflows, surrogate selection should be tied to the flow physics and validated with failure-mode-aware metrics rather than pointwise RMSE alone.
method: Compared 8 surrogate models on two transient flows: CMP slurry film and Karman vortex street.
Contrasted full-field vs latent representations and one-shot vs autoregressive time prediction.
Evaluated performance with five physics-based questions: field, structure, invented motion, amplitude, and timing.
evidence_signal: A one-shot full-field model achieved 3.2% relative error on cumulative wall shear stress for CMP, while a latent autoregressive DeepONet preserved 96% of vortex-shedding power in KVS where direct and one-shot models nearly eliminated it.
watch_item: The offline training cost is substantial, so the payoff depends on how many inference queries are needed beyond the training set.
paper_title: No Free Lunch in Flow Surrogates under Time-Varying Boundary Conditions: A Two-Regime Study
